n: If someone is caught in a sin, spiritually mature members should gently help restore him — keeping watch over themselves so they aren’t tempted too.

f.g: Greek katartizo — to mend, like setting a broken bone or repairing a net.

n: Carry each other’s burdens, and so fulfill Christ’s law of love.
Anyone who thinks he is something special when he is nothing is fooling himself.
Each should examine his own work. Then he can take satisfaction in it without comparing himself to others.
Each person must carry his own load of responsibility before God.

f.g: A different word from verse 2 — a personal pack every soldier carries.

n: Those taught the gospel should share good things with their teachers.
Don’t be fooled: God can’t be mocked. People reap what they sow.

f.w: whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap

n: Sow to selfish desires and you reap decay; sow to the Spirit and you reap eternal life.
Don’t get tired of doing good. At the right time we will reap a harvest if we don’t give up.

f.w: let us not be weary in well doing

n: Whenever we have the opportunity, do good to everyone — especially fellow members of the household of faith.
Paul takes the pen himself: see what large letters he uses as he writes in his own hand — perhaps for emphasis, or because of poor eyesight.
Those pushing circumcision want to look good outwardly and avoid persecution for preaching the cross of Christ.

f.w: a fair shew in the flesh

n: Even they don’t keep the whole law. They want the Galatians circumcised so they can boast about it.

f.g: Boast of your circumcision as a trophy.

n: Paul will boast only in the cross of Christ. Through it, the world is dead to him and he is dead to the world.

f.w: the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ
the world is crucified unto me

n: In Christ, being circumcised or not means nothing; what matters is becoming a new creation.
Peace and mercy on all who follow this rule — the true Israel of God, defined by faith in Christ.

f.g: God’s covenant people, Jew and Gentile united in Christ.

n: From now on, let no one trouble Paul, because he bears the scars of Jesus on his body — the marks of beatings and stoning endured for Christ.

f.w: the marks of the Lord Jesus
f.g: Greek stigmata — brand marks; here, his scars of persecution.

n: Paul closes with a blessing of Christ’s grace on their spirits, addressing them warmly as brothers and sisters.

f.w: the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ
